post.title: What really happens if you stop paying rent?
post.ig:
An eviction case can follow you for 7 years.
Landlords filed 1.23 million eviction cases in 2025 across the areas Princeton's Eviction Lab tracks.
The usual path (rules vary by state): late fee, pay-or-quit notice (example: 3 days in California, 14 in New York), lawsuit, judgment, removal by a sheriff or marshal.
Credit reports generally leave evictions off, but unpaid rent sent to collections can stay up to 7 years. Tenant screening reports can list eviction cases for up to 7 years (CFPB).
In 2023, TransUnion paid $15 million to settle FTC and CFPB allegations it misreported eviction records. Local legal aid or 211 can explain local rules.
Sources: Eviction Lab (Apr 2026), CFPB, FTC, Experian, CA Attorney General, NY CourtHelp.
News and education, not financial advice.

post.yt_desc:
What happens if you stop paying rent? Rules vary by state, but the usual path runs from a late fee and a pay-or-quit notice to a lawsuit, a judgment and removal by a sheriff or marshal. Landlords filed 1.23 million eviction cases in 2025 across areas tracked by Princeton's Eviction Lab, and the CFPB says eviction cases can stay on tenant screening reports for up to 7 years. Sources: Eviction Lab, CFPB, FTC, Experian. News and education, not financial advice.
